title: Data visualization color palettes
when: The user builds charts, graphs, maps or dashboards and needs colors for series, ranges or positive and negative values.
inputs: the data and what it compares
prompt:
Goal: Chart colors that match the data type (categorical, sequential, diverging), work for color blind readers and are labeled directly.
Steps:
1. Classify the data: categories (unordered), sequential (low to high), diverging (around a midpoint such as zero or a target).
2. Categorical: up to 6 hues of similar lightness, ordered so neighbors contrast; fold the rest into Other in gray.
3. Sequential: one hue from light to dark in 5 to 7 even lightness steps; darker means more.
4. Diverging: two hues on either side of a light neutral midpoint, equal steps each way.
5. Avoid red next to green; prefer blue with orange, and add direct labels, shapes or patterns so color is not the only cue.
6. Highlight by saturation: the focus series in full color, others in muted gray.
Quality bar:
- Each series is named on or next to its mark.
- Marks reach 3 to 1 against the chart background.
- No rainbow scale for ordered data.
Pitfalls:
- Ten categorical colors.
- Red and green as the only difference.
- Pale yellow bars on white.
Verify:
- [ ] Palette type matches the data.
- [ ] Series colors are :root tokens.
- [ ] Axis and label text use the text color.
- [ ] Direct labels or patterns exist.
Output: Chart color tokens in style.css and their use in the chart script or SVG.

examples.input: cores para o grafico de vendas por regiao
examples.output: 5 categorical tokens of equal lightness, gray Other, direct labels at line ends, blue and orange for the two main series
